name: a_semis_supply
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: Semis & supply chain.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
TSMC / Samsung / SK hynix / Micron / Intel news; wafer and memory (DRAM, NAND, HBM) pricing; chip supply/demand estimates; equipment orders; supply-chain reports (Nikkei, DigiTimes, TrendForce, CLSA); China chip probes and export-control actions.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **TSM** — Fab & Foundry
- TSMC reported third-quarter net profit of NT$763.1 billion, up 69% year over year and above the NT$746.3 billion LSEG SmartEstimate; quarterly revenue was US$46.72 billion, up 50% year over year. (Reuters, Oct. 15; publication time not reported)[1]
- TSMC guided fourth-quarter revenue to US$52.3 billion–US$54.3 billion, versus US$33.73 billion a year earlier. (Reuters, Oct. 15; publication time not reported)[1]
- TSMC raised its 2026 full-year revenue-growth outlook to approximately 44%, from more than 40% previously. (Reuters, Oct. 15; publication time not reported)[5]
- TSMC kept 2026 capital spending guidance at US$60 billion–US$64 billion. (Reuters, Oct. 15; publication time not reported)[1]
- TSMC said high-performance computing represented 68% of third-quarter revenue, while 3-nanometer and 2-nanometer processes together accounted for 41% of wafer revenue. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15 12:29 ET)[3]
- TSMC reported third-quarter gross margin of 66.4% and guided fourth-quarter gross margin to 65%–67%. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15 12:26 ET)[6]
- TSMC said demand for leading-edge technologies was “extremely robust,” but described its 2027 planning outlook as cautious because of macroeconomic uncertainty. (Reuters, Oct. 15; publication time not reported)[1]
- TSMC said it was discussing participation in Elon Musk’s Terafab project in Texas, with any arrangement requiring TSMC to operate the plant. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15 12:29 ET)[2]
- TSMC’s U.S.-listed shares were reported down more than 2% premarket; Taiwan-listed shares closed down 2% on Oct. 15. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15 12:29 ET; publication time not reported)[2][3]

## **005930 / Samsung Electronics** — Memory & Interconnect
- Samsung Electronics shares fell more than 10% after TSMC’s results and outlook were reported. (Reuters, Oct. 15; publication time not reported)[1]
- Samsung Electronics shares were reported down 5.17% at 220,000 won early on Oct. 15. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15; publication time not reported)[9]

## **000660 / SK hynix** — Memory & Interconnect
- SK hynix shares fell more than 10% after TSMC’s earnings report and 2027 caution. (Reuters, Oct. 15; publication time not reported)[1]
- SK hynix shares were reported down 11.06% at 1,262,000 won at mid-session on Oct. 15. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15; publication time not reported)[9]

## **MU / Memory** — Memory & Interconnect
- Micron shares were reported down more than 3% in premarket trading on Oct. 15 amid a broader AI-infrastructure and semiconductor selloff. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15; publication time not reported)[7]
- The available reports did not provide an in-window Micron earnings, pricing, supply, demand, or guidance update.

## **INTC / Intel** — Fab & Foundry
- Intel shares were reported down more than 3% in premarket trading on Oct. 15 amid the semiconductor selloff. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15; publication time not reported)[7]
- TSMC already operates an Austin facility, while Intel was identified as a partner with a facility on South MoPac Expressway in connection with the proposed Texas Terafab project. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15 12:29 ET)[2]
- The available reports did not provide an in-window Intel earnings, order, capacity, or export-control update.

## **NVDA / AMD / AVGO** — AI Compute
- Nvidia and AMD shares were reported down more than 2% and 3%, respectively, during the Oct. 15 semiconductor selloff; Broadcom also declined. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15; publication time not reported)[9]
- TSMC identified Nvidia, AMD, and Broadcom as customers for advanced processors manufactured on its leading-edge processes. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15 12:26 ET)[6]

## **SNDK** — Memory & Interconnect
- Sandisk shares were reported down more than 4% in premarket trading on Oct. 15. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15; publication time not reported)[7]
- The available reports did not provide an in-window Sandisk NAND pricing, supply, demand, or guidance update.

## Semiconductors — Macro / Commodities
- The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported September wholesale prices up 1.3% month over month and 6.3% year over year, versus a 5.5% economist projection cited in market coverage. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15; publication time not reported)[7]
- Korea Exchange suspended program trading shortly after the Oct. 15 open after benchmark futures breached the exchange’s trigger. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15; publication time not reported)[9]
- The available search results contained no reportable in-window wafer, DRAM, NAND, HBM pricing, semiconductor-equipment order, China chip-probe, or new export-control action.
